A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Is Complex Query Answering Really Complex? Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark-distribution analyses, stratified model evaluations, CQD-Hybrid experiments, and evaluations on three constructed benchmarks in Sections 4–6 and appendices A and D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports CLMPT evaluations and statistical comparisons in Appendix D.2.

M1.justification: CQD-Hybrid retains the same procedure: combine neural link prediction with maximal scores for observed training links. Benchmark construction and query-reduction procedures are retained. Added implementation explanations and the CLMPT comparator do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FB15k237, NELL995, their +H variants, and ICEWS18+H, including union, negation, and four-link query types. Negation results incorporated into v3 Table 5 already appear in v2 Appendix D. DAG and multiple-target extensions remain future work.

E2.justification: v3 adds CLMPT to the principal comparisons and stratified appendix evaluations across the retained benchmarks. The existing comparator set remains; QTO was already evaluated in v2, and FIT still receives no separate evaluation.

E3.justification: The added CLMPT experiments introduce ICEWS18+H training with learning-rate and temperature selection. Appendix G.2.2 also narrows the stated per-triple validation/test generation rule to 1p, whereas v2 attached it to 1p, 2in, and 2nu1p. This reported protocol revision does not establish regenerated data; existing splits, MRR, and sampling quotas remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2 examines whether models with close aggregate MRR nevertheless differ statistically, first for FB15k237+H 2p queries and then across all its query types. Existing cardinality, anchor/relation imbalance, union-filtering, and hardness-stratification analyses are retained, with CLMPT added to several comparisons.

E5.justification: v2 provides no formal significance testing. v3 introduces pairwise Mann–Whitney U tests on reciprocal ranks, a complete p-value matrix for FB15k237+H 2p queries in Table D.2, and a reported pooled-query analysis. This substantially adds statistical reporting, although neither version reports seeds, repeated-run variability, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Extensive new CLMPT scores change several reported leaders: for NELL995+H 2i, v2 Table 4's best is ConE at 21.8, while v3 Table 5 adds CLMPT at 22.7. CQD-Hybrid's comparison win count changes from 10/14 to 9/14. v3 also fills QTO's missing NELL995 3i-to-2i entry with 12.4 and adds statistical-test outcomes. These are added comparisons and entries, not demonstrated improvements to an unchanged model.

T1.justification: The query formulas, reasoning-tree and partial/full-inference definitions, MRR expression, and appendix formulations are retained. v3 adds no theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or revised formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and stated contributions retain the same scientific claims about reducible queries, inflated apparent performance, memorization, CQD-Hybrid, and harder benchmarks. Added concluding emphasis reiterates these claims; the more explicit recommendation to adopt the benchmarks does not establish a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new statistical tests as showing different ranking behavior despite similar MRR, while describing selected nonsignificant comparisons as statistical similarity. The conclusion adds DAG-structured queries as a future extension and explicitly encourages benchmark adoption. Existing memorization explanations and single-target limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds negation hyperparameters and the standard-negation choice, documents 4p/4i settings and CQD-Hybrid's 64 beam upper bound for 4p, and supplies QTO/CLMPT configuration sources and CLMPT tuning details. These mainly fill documentation gaps. Code, data, and generation scripts were already linked in v2.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and discussion for CLMPT and LMPNN, Ruffinelli et al. on inherited benchmark practices, and Arun, Yin, and He et al. on possible extensions. This updates comparator context and future-work positioning without replacing the paper's central relationship to earlier CQA research.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose and terminology edits, standardizes references to QA pairs, clarifies union filtering and sampling, expands implementation explanations, and adds a statistical subsection. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The union illustration moves from v2 Figure A.1 to v3 Figure 3, and the hybrid comparison moves from Table A.3 to main-text Table 3 with a revised arrangement. Table 5 becomes full-width and incorporates existing appendix negation scores. Comparator rows, hyperparameter columns, and a new p-value table are added; the underlying plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, CLMPT comparisons strengthen empirical coverage, Appendix F fills reproducibility gaps, and relocated displays make supporting evidence easier to find. These are useful, limited gains. The new statistical section reduces their strength by ambiguously describing a 'paired Mann–Whitney' test and interpreting nonsignificance as similarity, so its addition does not establish a substantial improvement in rigor.
